summary.headline: Mold-Tek H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 18.62 crore, about 4.7x the prior-year H1, with standalone Q2 PAT of INR 10.16 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported strong Q2 FY27 numbers: standalone Q2 turnover of INR 46.64 crore (up 25% YoY) and PAT of INR 10.16 crore versus INR 3.15 crore a year earlier, with standalone H1 PAT of about INR 20 crore. Consolidated H1 PAT was INR 18.62 crore against INR 10 crore for full FY26. Management attributed the gains to product mix, operational efficiency, and higher-value engineering services in poles and towers and structural steel detailing. The BIW segment has been cut sharply, and the Beryl acquisition is still loss-making (about USD 25,000 loss in Q2) with breakeven targeted for Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 3.15 crore in Q2 FY26 (more than 3x)
vs gain of INR 1.5 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: Manpower contribution INR 5,220 per head (Q2) vs INR 4,500 in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Structural steel detailing and civil structural work (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said about 75-80% of revenue comes from structural steel detailing and related areas, roughly USD 4.4-5.3 million of H1 work (about 80-82%). Connection design is tracking toward about USD 1 million this year.

segments.name: Poles, towers and power distribution (utility fixed teams, MAS)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 30-40 people last year to 70-75 now, with a target of 120 by March 2027 against fixed-team demand of 110-125. Management said there is a severe shortage of talent in this skill set.

segments.name: BIW / automotive (MES)
segments.commentary: Revenue from MES automobile services has fallen to about USD 100,000 in the quarter. BIW headcount was cut from 150-160 to about 50, with a further 5-10 possible reduction and 20-25 people being retrained.

segments.name: Beryl (US subsidiary, acquired about 9-10 months ago)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making, with a loss of about USD 25,000 in Q2 versus USD 70,000-75,000 in Q1. A USD 1 million Hillsborough County design order was received in October, and breakeven is targeted for Q3.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated top-line growth of at least 18-20% and standalone growth of about 20-25% over the next 12-18 months, subject to dollar movements.
Management expects a further 15% productivity gain without a large headcount increase, which could take revenue per employee to about USD 35,000 per year.
Beryl expected to turn positive in Q3 FY27 (breakeven) and to contribute meaningfully in FY28.
Poles and towers growth expected from Q3 or Q4, with the ramp-up of fixed teams to 120 by March 2027.
Civil and land development work with a US client expected to become sizable from January-February 2027; an MOU is already signed.
Management gave no quantitative FY28 margin guidance. It said the company should stay on a positive track for the next one to two years.
capex_capacity: Utility fixed-team headcount is planned to rise from about 70-75 to 120 by March 2027. Some 40-45 people are in training, and the MSA is for 25 people, with 10-15 currently offered.
BIW headcount is being reduced to a nominal size, with outsourcing of residual work to small players planned.
Beryl's design team is centred on six engineers, with a five-person team in Hyderabad supporting a design head based in Tampa.
Automation and tooling are being introduced to lift output and quality. Management said no large recruitment is needed and that hiring will be project-driven.
Management is open to an acquisition of a US structural design firm but is not satisfied with the current candidate and is considering other targets. No decision has been made.
demand_pricing: Work on hand fell to about USD 4.2 million from USD 4.5 million in Q1, but October brought record bookings and the level is now above end-June.
Data centre engineering: 5-6 projects completed over the past 1-2 years, with 2-3 on hand now. Each project is about USD 300-500k.
Management said US outsourcing of core civil and mechanical engineering will keep growing given local engineer shortages.
Management said structural design commands higher hourly rates than detailing, and expects residential, architectural and civil work to carry much higher fees than steel detailing.
The rupee was stabilising around USD 95 per dollar, which management expects to yield forex gains in Q3 if it holds.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the EBITDA margin and profitability, and is there FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the BIW loss-making segment has been removed and the EV/automotive volatility eliminated. It expects positive performance for the next one to two years, with Beryl and new civil and land work adding to growth. No quantitative FY28 guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did work on hand fall QoQ, and what is the segment mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Work on hand fell to USD 4.2 million from USD 4.5 million, but October bookings were a record. Structural steel detailing is 75-80% of revenue, with civil structural about 80-82% of standalone revenue and MES automotive services down to about USD 100,000.

qa_highlights.question: What are the forex gain/loss and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 had a forex loss of about INR 70 lakh versus a gain of INR 1.5 crore in Q1. Management said operating profit growth would be 14-15% excluding forex and expects a gain in Q3 if the rupee holds near 95.

qa_highlights.question: When will Beryl reach breakeven and when will outsourcing to India start?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl's Q2 loss was about USD 25,000, down from USD 70-75k. Breakeven is targeted for Q3 and positive results from next year. A design head is in place in Tampa with a five-person team in Hyderabad, and full benefits are expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks with a prospective seller are ongoing, but management has concerns about the business and the seller's ability to scale. No confirmed decision has been made, and other options are being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Will the three-year fixed-team MSA carry committed volumes, and what capacity is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: The MSA is a fixed-team arrangement with a 25-person requirement, of which 10-15 are currently offered, with ramp-up by end-November or December. Management said incremental recruitment will be client-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Would an AI or data-centre slowdown hit the poles and data-centre business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said data centres are only one of many high-rise and commercial projects, so a slowdown would not hit detailing drastically. For utilities, growth could taper from the planned 70 to 125 people, but current performance rests on about 70 engineers.

risks_watch: Beryl must reach breakeven in Q3 FY27 as guided, having been loss-making for two to three quarters.
Utility fixed-team ramp to 120 people by March 2027 depends on training and talent availability. Demand is tied to US data-centre and power-grid build-out.
Dollar and forex swings. Q2 had a forex loss of about INR 70 lakh, and Q3 expectations depend on the rupee holding near USD 95.
Work on hand fell QoQ to USD 4.2 million, so order-book conversion needs monitoring.
Any acquisition is unresolved, and the target and valuation are undisclosed. Management said it would not let deal costs affect the numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the standalone turnaround and productivity, with specific numbers given. Cautious and less specific on Beryl's timing, the civil and land development ramp, and the acquisition, which management said is unresolved. Management sidestepped the question on valuation and deal terms.
key_quotes: So, overall put together, whatever disturbances or ups and downs caused by electrical vehicle and our automobile team will be removed for the future.
So there is no need for huge recruitments going forward. That will be client driven or project-to-project driven.
We definitely want to stay at the designing and detailing. We don't want to become an EPC and take up the construction and monitoring because that will be too much of responsibility.

adds.what: Utility poles/towers fixed-team headcount ramp from about 70-75 to 120 by March 2027 (people, not plant capacity)

growth.why: Management holds consolidated top-line growth of at least 18-20% and standalone 20-25% over 12-18 months, backed by fixed-team ramp from 70-75 to 120 by March 2027 (against 110-125 demand), a USD 1m Hillsborough order and work on hand of USD 4.2m with record October bookings, though work on hand fell QoQ and no capex or quantified capacity was given.
